lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text:
A caddy to hold jerry cans of petrol in a car boot cannot be built safely in Hex Cluster.

**Why this request is declined:**
* The parts are 3D-printed plastic and the configurator only checks fit and collisions. It does not know about material strength, load ratings, fuel resistance, heat, or crash safety.
* Petrol is a flammable fuel. A printed caddy cannot safely restrain heavy liquid fuel containers in a moving vehicle - in braking, cornering or a collision the load, spillage, fumes and fire risk require a purpose-made, tested metal restraint, not a plastic print.
* A build that would hold fuel or anything burning/hot is listed as unsafe to build as asked.

Nothing has been placed.

I can instead build a safe compromise if you want - for example:
* a general boot organiser / caddy for cold tools, groceries, or workshop bottles (non-fuel)
* a garage storage caddy for empty, clean jerry cans kept upright outside the vehicle, with no fuel

If you want one of those alternatives, tell me which and I will build it.
